newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan traders see PGM mkt squeeze by hedge funds.
newsitem.headline: Japan traders see PGM mkt squeeze by hedge funds.

text.p: Platinum group metal (PGM) prices are expected to be extremely volatile in the short-term due to suspected attempts by U.S. hedge funds to squeeze the market, precious metal traders said on Thursday.
"I'm really puzzled by the skyrocketing PGM prices and lease rates. Market movements are no longer connected to the Russian factor," one trader with a trading house said.

"PGM prices should have fallen as Russia's resumption of exports are looming on the horizon. It's manipulation (by U.S. funds) to squeeze the market," he said, adding prices hinge on when U.S. funds decide to liquidate their longs.

Spot palladium extended overnight gains to be quoted at $220.00/230.00 per ounce at 0521 GMT, against $210 on Wednesday in London, where a rally took the rare metal to its highest since fixings started in 1989.
Spot platinum stood at $420.00/245.00, against $427.00/437.00 in London on Wednesday.
"It's possible that palladium will move between $100 and $300 (per ounce), depending on the volume of Russian sales and funds' move," one precious metal industry source said.
Some traders said there was market talk that the CFTC (Commodities Futures Trading Commission) may investigate the NYMEX palladium market for possible manipulation.
"Some traders say it would be no surprise if the CFTC intervened in the market," the first trader said.
Worries about delays to supply from Russia have caused PGM prices to rally in recent months.
However, traders said such worries had been alleviated as ongoing 1997 term contract talks between Japanese clients and the Russian PGM export agency were progressing smoothly.
Russian officials have told Japanese clients that exports would begin around June 20, and that Russia has enough supplies for all of its customers.
Traders said they were growing increasingly concerned about speculative trade in overseas futures markets.
"It's sad. It would be easy to squeeze the PGM market as it is so small," one official of a bullion house said.
The February issue of "Institutional Investor" magazine said hedge fund Tiger Management, run by Julian Robertson, had been buying "tons of palladium recently".
"At some point -- I don't know when -- all these people are going to be asking, where are we going to get our palladium," the magazine quoted Robertson as saying. "And the only place will be us."
Traders, however, said bearish signals, such as a steep backwardation in TOCOM platinum and palladium futures prices and record high PGM lease rates, were emerging.

"Surging spot market prices forced private investors to cover massive shorts in nearby TOCOM months, while there is little buying in distant months in anticipation of a sharp fall later in the year," an analyst at a commodity broker said.
Short-term palladium lease rates rocketed to 150 percent today, while platinum lease rates stood at 50-60 percent. The normal lease rates for both metals are two or three percent.
"People are unwilling to buy palladium now because they expect prices will fall when Russia resumes exports," the analyst said.
Traders said the recent rise in Rhodium prices was the result of a combination of factors, such as an increase in auto catalyst demand in Japan and falling domestic rhodium stocks.
Soaring platinum and palladium prices were also hauling rhodium higher, traders said.
